summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Aurora GPU Systems to explore channel partnership and technical integration for private / dedicated inference. Key topics: integration points (API vs private control plane), network/VPC constraints, model compatibility, benchmarking plan, commercial motion for reseller/partner credits.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 15:00 UTC / Duration ~54m / Attendees: Ava, Samir, Jules (Redwood); Liam, Rosa, Miguel, Priya (Aurora)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro + discovery; high level tech overlap; agree to run bench and test private deployment flow; send docs and schedule deep dive.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE covering partnerships; with me Samir our SE and Jules from partnerships. Quick round-robin?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): Hey Ava, Liam here, Head of Partnerships at Aurora. Rosa, Miguel, Priya are on. Appreciate you all making time.
00:20 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Hi! thanks.
00:23 Speaker 2 (Liam): The goal for us is to get into the partner program and understand how Aurora hardware could be offered as a preferred infra option for Redwood customers, also any white-label or resale possibilities.
00:35 Speaker 1 (Ava): Great. High level we'll cover a bit about Redwood's deployment modes — hosted API, Dedicated, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — then explore integration points and where Aurora fits. Samir, wanna give a quick tech overview?
00:48 Speaker 4 (Samir): Sure; hey all. Redwood's inference runtime is GPU optimized, we do continuous batching, KV caching, kernel selection — some customers call that the "KV cash" which is wrong but, you know — and we support model variants including quantized ones and routing policies. For partners like Aurora we usually look at two flows: one, Aurora as a hardware provider for Redwood Dedicated pools; two, Aurora as a customer option for Redwood Private where we deploy control plane pieces in a VPC on the customer side.
01:15 Speaker 5 (Miguel): A couple clarifying questions up front: when you say "control plane" in private, is that still managed by Redwood or fully stateless so we can host in our region? We have customers who need air-gapped options.
01:29 Speaker 4 (Samir): Good question. We have a private deployment pattern where the control plane can be hosted in the customer's VPC with connectors back to Redwood for billing/console, or we can do a fully on-prem package for air-gapped customers. There's some hybrid options.
01:42 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Ok, hybrid might work. From our side, network egress and management plane auth are the sticky bits — we run strict firewall policies.
01:52 Speaker 1 (Ava): Noted. We'll need Aurora's infra diagram and network constraints, Priya?\01:57 Speaker 6 (Priya): Yep we'll share that. Our main requirements: SAML/SSO, KMS integration for customer keys, and audit logs. SOC2 is common ask from our enterprise buyers.
02:08 Speaker 4 (Samir): We have SAML/SO, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. We can map to Aurora's requirements — sometimes customers want their KMS only which we support via customer-managed keys.
02:20 Speaker 2 (Liam): On GTM — what's the typical partner revenue split or referral model? We don't expect to be an MSP reselling day one but want clarity.
02:29 Speaker 1 (Ava): For partners we have a couple of motions: technology partner (co-marketing + preferred infra) and reseller/referral for dedicated setups. Commercials vary but typical early-stage partner credits are available — we'll share a partner playbook.
02:40 Speaker 5 (Miguel): On the technical side, what's the compatibility with Aurora's GPU SKUs? We run a mix of A100-like and more cost-efficient Ampere/Grace combos.
02:51 Speaker 4 (Samir): Our runtime supports a range; we publish performance profiles per architecture. For benchmarking we usually pick representative models (e.g., 7B v1, 13B, and one LLM-ops model for longer context) and test latency, throughput, cost per token. Some nuance: quantized paths can differ by GPU (tensor core support etc.).
03:13 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Could you share an example benchmark spreadsheet?
03:16 Speaker 4 (Samir): Yes, we'll send our bench template — includes seq lengths, batch sizes, perf numbers, and reference datasets. We'll flag where kernel choices may differ; sometimes the name of a kernel gets slightly mangled in logs like "mmult" vs "matmul" so don't be surprised.
03:30 Speaker 2 (Liam): What about orchestration — do you expect us to provide a turnkey node image or we plug into Redwood's agent?
03:38 Speaker 4 (Samir): We usually need a node image with drivers and CUDA runtime set, plus our agent container. For Dedicated we manage the scheduling layer and autoscaling; for Private, the agent runs on customer-managed nodes and reports to the private control plane.
03:55 Speaker 6 (Priya): On security, do you have SOC2 reports and pen test summaries we can share with buyers?
04:02 Speaker 1 (Ava): Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and some compliance artifacts. We'll share a redacted package through the partner portal.
04:10 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Latency vs cost question — our customers ask whether Redwood will prefer lower-latency instance types or cheaper high-density instances; how does routing choose?
04:22 Speaker 4 (Samir): Routing is policy-driven; Redwood can route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. For partner-hosted capacity, we can include Aurora's pools as an option and set fallbacks. Some customers prefer dedicated low-latency, others prefer bursty cost-optimized routing.
04:37 Speaker 2 (Liam): How much engineering effort to onboard an Aurora cluster?
04:41 Speaker 4 (Samir): Onboarding time varies: Dedicated on Aurora-managed pools is quicker — maybe 2-4 weeks for initial tests, 4-8 weeks for production depending on networking and certs. Private with tight firewall rules may take longer.
04:55 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Any case studies of partners bringing capacity to market?
05:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): We have a few partners — we can introduce you to a partner success story, will include that in the deck.
05:07 Speaker 2 (Liam): Cool. On the technical deep dive we'd want to bring our infra ops and networking folks. Can we scope a runbook for the bench?
05:16 Speaker 4 (Samir): Absolutely. Typical bench steps: 1) agree models/seq lengths, 2) provision nodes + image, 3) run baseline on Aurora with raw model, 4) run quantized/optimized variants, 5) test failure/fallback scenarios. We'll define metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, and cost per 1M tokens.
05:38 Speaker 6 (Priya): For private deployments, do you ship an operator? We run k8s clusters but some customers still prefer VM-based setups.
05:46 Speaker 4 (Samir): We support k8s and VM deployments. There are small differences in autoscaling hooks. We'll note VM runbook if that's your primary.
06:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): Single-tenant vs multi-tenant — do you co-locate multiple customers on the same GPU? Some enterprise buyers ask for physical isolation.
06:09 Speaker 4 (Samir): Dedicated pools can be single-tenant; multi-tenant is typical for hosted API. For strict isolation customers we recommend Dedicated or Private.
06:18 Speaker 5 (Miguel): About metrics and observability — Redwood Console, does it surface token-level cost, per-model dashboards?
06:25 Speaker 4 (Samir): Yes, Redwood Console shows per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traces, and error analysis. You can hook in external tracing too.
06:35 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Will there be a partner listing in your console or marketplace?
06:38 Speaker 1 (Ava): We're working on a partner marketplace; initial partners get co-marketing placements. We'll share the timeline.
06:45 Speaker 2 (Liam): Any IP concerns if we share performance numbers publicly?
06:48 Speaker 1 (Ava): We can coordinate messaging; we'll agree on co-branded content and approvals.
07:00 Speaker 6 (Priya): Network ports and certs — for private control plane what ports need to be open outbound?
07:07 Speaker 4 (Samir): Generally HTTPS outbound to control endpoints, and a few specific ports for agent telemetry — we'll put that in the runbook.
07:15 Speaker 2 (Liam): How do you handle model updates and version pinning for a customer in Redwood Private?
07:21 Speaker 4 (Samir): Customers can pin model versions, we support rollout policies (canary, A/B tests) and automatic fallback to compatible variants. That's important for enterprise change control.
07:34 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Cost model for Dedicated — do you do monthly reserved capacity or usage-based?
07:40 Speaker 1 (Ava): Dedicated is typically reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. Hosted API is usage-based. For reseller agreements we can discuss special pricing.
07:50 Speaker 2 (Liam): Is there an eval program or credits we can use for initial bench runs?
07:54 Speaker 1 (Ava): Yes, partners often get partner credits for initial benchmarking. We'll include details.
08:05 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Ok if we hand off to Samir to scope the bench, we'll loop in Miguel's ops.
08:10 Speaker 4 (Samir): Sounds good. I'll outline a bench plan after the call.

08:22 Speaker 1 (Ava): Quick note — some of our customers require data residency in EU, do Aurora regions include EU zones?
08:30 Speaker 2 (Liam): We have EU sites in Frankfurt and Amsterdam, yes.
08:35 Speaker 5 (Miguel): On encryption at rest, how do you integrate KMS with our HSM?
08:40 Speaker 4 (Samir): We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations, and can support HSM-backed KMS if Aurora exposes standard APIs. We'll need some partner engineering work there.
08:50 Speaker 6 (Priya): We also need to check licensing for certain models; some open models have license clauses.
08:56 Speaker 4 (Samir): Agreed; we'll include our model catalog and license notes — sometimes we recommend model variants with permissive licenses.
09:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): How aggressive is your batching? Some customers worry batching increases tail latency.
09:12 Speaker 4 (Samir): We do continuous batching tuned to latency SLOs; customers configure batching windows and max batch sizes. Batching reduces cost but we tune to keep p95 within SLO.
09:24 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Can you do a demo of the Console in the deep dive?
09:27 Speaker 1 (Ava): Yes, we'll do that in the next meeting.

09:35 Speaker 2 (Liam): A couple of potential blockers: cert rotation and CA requirements for certain gov customers.
09:42 Speaker 4 (Samir): We can support cert rotation policies and custom CA bundles for private deployments. We'll need to document requirements.
09:50 Speaker 5 (Miguel): SLA expectations — what uptime guarantees for Dedicated?
09:54 Speaker 1 (Ava): Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share specifics in docs.
10:02 Speaker 6 (Priya): Okay what's the timeline — if we try a pilot, when could we realistically get a POC up?
10:09 Speaker 1 (Ava): If we align quickly and you provide infra details, we can aim to start a bench within 2 weeks and have a POC (non-prod) in 4-6 weeks.
10:17 Speaker 2 (Liam): Works for us. We'll prioritize the infra diagram and contact for ops.
10:22 Speaker 1 (Ava): Great. Next steps recap at about 40: we already listed some items but I'll recap at the end too.

10:30 Speaker 4 (Samir): One more technical note: for model quantization we sometimes rely on specific CUDA ops; older GPU drivers can cause differences — ensure node images include the tested driver versions.
10:45 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Noted. We'll standardize images.

11:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): Ok let's go through next steps and owners: I'll send the partner deck and SOC2/tech docs, Samir will send bench plan, Liam will share infra diagram. Anything else?
11:12 Speaker 2 (Liam): Please include sample partner agreement.
11:15 Speaker 1 (Ava): Will do.
11:18 Speaker 3 (Rosa): Also please include an estimated commercial sheet — high-level numbers for Dedicated and referral.
11:22 Speaker 1 (Ava): We'll add that as a range.

11:30 Speaker 1 (Ava): Thanks everyone — we'll aim to follow up by Friday with all artifacts and propose times for the technical deep dive.
11:36 Speaker 2 (Liam): Thanks, talk soon.
11:40 Speaker 6 (Priya): Bye.

(End of recording)
